recipes.name: Guinness Beer Cheese Dip
ingredients_raw: 32 ounces processed cheese food (such as Velveeta®), cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 cup Irish stout beer (such as Guinness®)

steps.text: Heat cheese in slow cooker on High until melted, about 20 minutes.
Stir beer, salsa, Worcestershire sauce, chili powder, onion powder, and cayenne pepper into cheese until smooth and heated through, stirring frequently, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Guinness Beer Cheese Dip
raw_recipe.description: This savory beer cheese dip made with Velveeta and flavored with salsa, stout beer, chili, and cayenne is a superb spicy warm dip perfect for parties.

video.description: If you’re fan of beer cheese soup, grab a tortilla chip, a pretzel or a hunk of sourdough and dip into this tasty crowd-calling showstopper!  Preparation couldn’t be easier, so if you’re invited to the party last-minute, you’ll still arrive as the star. Begin by melting cheese in the slow cooker, then stir in Irish stout beer, salsa, Worcestershire sauce, chili powder, onion powder and cayenne. Every cheesy bite will zing with peppery flavor!

review.reviewBody: I made this for our Christmas Eve drop in and it was a huge hit! My only change was to add in some smoked Gouda Cheese after reading another review, great suggestion. I served it with a loaf of cubed marble rye/pumpernickel bread and sour dough pretzels! I plan to make this again for a Super Bowl party!

We don’t have velveta cheese here in Sweden so I made a 50/50 mix of cream cheese and cheddar. Melt the cream cheese in a double boiler, or a metal bowl place over a por of boiling water. Then fold in an equal weight of fresh grated cheddar. Then when it’s all melted slowly stir in room temperature beer, and the remaining ingredients. Once everything is mixed together, let it cook for 10 minutes stirring frequently to prevent the top from drying out. This sauce can be used as a dip for soft pretzels, bread sticks, or nachos.

So very easy to make! Excellent for beginner chefs!! 30 minutes or less in the crock pot and you have a great cheesy game-day-dip!!! Guilt set in as I had minimal effort, and by minimal, I mean: set the crock pot to heat, add ingredients, mix and stir and – TaDa! I served my dip with assorted tortilla chips, crackers, and vegetables. It was a crowd pleasure, even If the crowd was just two hungry people watching the Super Bowl. Three days later I was in the mood for a cheesy pasta dish. In a pan, I warmed up some heavy whipping cream, added 1 cup of the leftover Guinness beer cheese dip, ¼ cup pesto and ¼ cup spaghetti sauce, ¼ cup each chopped zucchini and mushrooms. Served over rotini pasta. It was wonderful!

Fantastic, huge hit at the party! I took out about 5 oz of the Velveeta and replaced it with a wedge of smoked Gouda with bacon, gave it just a hint of smoky flavor. Just personal preference, I'm sure that strictly adhering to the recipe as written would not have changed my opinion :)

Excellent recipe, it was a huge hit at our house, and the leftovers were used for days for everything from nachos to scrambled eggs! The only tweak I made to the recipe is I added about 4x the amount of salsa to it and let it cook down in the slow cooker for a few hours. It still had that robust flavor from the Guinness and Worcestershire sauce but the tomotatoes and spices from the salsa gave it some complexity and a little more “zip”. Thanks for sharing your recipe! Definitely will make this one again.

The crowd(s) loved it. Yes, it was slow to melt, but pouring a little of the leftover Guinness into the crockpot hurried the melting. It starts out *very* liquid in consistency, but thickens nicely. Served with soft pretzels Day 1, then offered as ‘Irish Queso’ for a taco bar on Day 2. Very well received both times.
Cut the recipe in half and it was perfect for us. Just the right amount of heat, although I did leave off the cayenne pepper
Made it with 4oz bourbon gouda and 24 oz. Velveeta, it was delicious
Really good and easy to make. I added the gouda and the bacon and it was very tasty. Adjustments for next time: use a little less beer and shred the gouda so it melts more easily.

This recipe, like most on here, is a great base. It goes great with everything. Ive put it on chicken, steak, used it to dip numerous breads and crackers in and haven’t found anything it isn’t good on. Here are my changes. I add 2-3 green onions (depending on the size), 1/2-3/4 of head of fresh garlic (again depends on size), and 2 jalapeños or serano peppers. I also add chipotle powder (about a tbsp). I feel this all compliments the recipe well and helps make it even better.
Super easy. Like others I swapped 8 oz smoked gouda. Everyone loved it. For St. Patty's Day I served with cut up Irish Soda Bread.
I wanted to love this dip. I was disappointed that I did not care for it. I think it must just be me because this is a really highly rated recipe. Thanks!!
Love this recipe as is. I have also use drained Rotel vs salsa with great results. Like to add mustard powder too! Will add this to dip rotations for sure!
It was good. I didn't have any salsa. Next time I will make sure I have some.
Easy peasy- brought to a church potluck with Fritos and pretzels.
Everyone loves it!! I’ve been making this one a while, it’s a keeper and one I go back to over and over
Excellent, served with Mini Tatar tots! Big hit!

This dip/sauce was Great! Cut the recipe in half and used it as a sauce on our Bratwurst Sandwiches. It was a hit with everyone. Will try it on the soft pretzels and will also use it as a sauce when I make fried potatoes and onions.

Agreed with what some other people have said about mixing in some other cheeses. Other than that this is perfect. I do not often like the taste of beer in food, this really is a perfect dip. Had it with soft pretzels.
This dip was huge hit at men’s night gather. Never had a chance to make past that night. Goes great with soft pretzels.
